extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from primary XML/PDF/SI locators; no unsupported cell-wall or protein-target mechanism was promoted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: C12/C14/C16-fXXL penetrate bacterial-model lipid monolayers and change molecular ordering in Langmuir monolayer experiments.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: C12-fXXL, C14-fXXL, C16-fXXL in POPE/DPPG/POPG and POPG/DPPG/CL monolayers
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model monolayer evidence supports membrane interaction; it is not a direct bacterial-cell molecular target assay.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: AFM supported-bilayer experiments support membrane thinning/fluidization after lipopeptide exposure, stronger in Gram-positive lipid-film mimics.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: model lipid bilayers exposed to C12/C14/C16-fXXL
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model bilayer data are mechanistic support for membrane activity but do not identify a specific protein/cell-wall target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Biological activity is strongest against Gram-positive staphylococci in Table 3, while C14-fXXL shows strong growth-inhibition dynamics in selected growth curves.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MIC Table 3 and bacterial growth Figures 6-7
mechanism_claims.limitations: Growth inhibition supports antimicrobial phenotype; exact curve point values were not digitized beyond prose/table values.

caution_findings.evidence_context: Membrane-active mechanism is supported by model membrane monolayer/bilayer assays plus phenotype, not direct bacterial-cell target identification.
Figures 6-8 provide image/curve evidence; final artifacts retain table/prose values and do not invent exact curve points.
